maya: Hey folks — running into two related issues with our Node SSE client: 1) JSON objects get split across chunks and the parser chokes (partial JSON errors), and 2) under sustained load the client stalls / stops emitting events (looks like a slow-consumer/backpressure problem). Using node-fetch + eventsource-polyfill. Any quick patterns or SDK flags people recommend?

sam: Can you paste the exact error/logs you see? Also: is auth being refreshed mid-stream?

maya: Logs (truncated):
```
ERROR: Unexpected end of JSON input at parse (parser.js:45)
stream: chunk #12345: "{\"id\":\"abc\", \"choices\": [ { \"text\": \"part1\" }"\nthen no event for ~8s and reconnects: 
WARN: reconnecting due to socket closed (code=1006)
ERROR: stream stalled: consumer queue length=1024
```

akiko: Two separate things usually: parser buffer handling and consumer backpressure. For the parser: accumulate bytes until you detect a full NDJSON line or a delimiter (we use double-newline `\n\n` for SSE event boundaries) and only JSON.parse completed segments. For backpressure: pause the underlying readable stream when your internal queue exceeds a threshold, resume when it drains. Example pseudo: 
```js
let buf = '';
reader.on('data', chunk => {
  buf += chunk;
  while (buf.includes('\n\n')) {
    const [line, rest] = buf.split(/\n\n/, 2);
    buf = rest;
    try { handle(JSON.parse(line)); } catch(e) { metrics.increment('parse_errors'); }
  }
  if (queue.length > MAX_QUEUE) { reader.pause(); setTimeout(() => reader.resume(), PAUSE_MS); }
});
```

jordan: Re: auth — we saw tokens expiring mid-stream before. Our refresh flow triggered immediate reconnects and that cascaded. Are you queueing events during a reconnect or dropping?

maya: We attempt to reconnect immediately on 401, but we don't debounce reconnects. On rapid failures we end up with many concurrent reconnect attempts.

sam: Two quick mitigations: (1) add exponential backoff + jitter for reconnects, with a short cooldown window after N rapid reconnects; (2) add a small circuit breaker that fails fast if parse_error rate > X in Y seconds so the system can back off instead of thrashing. Also limit concurrent reconns per route (eg max_concurrent_reconnects=2).

maya: Are there any SDK config knobs I should try first instead of rewriting client logic?

akiko: In the client SDK we expose a few options (these names are current in the branch so check your SDK version):
```json
{
  "max_buffered_messages": 200,
  "pause_on_backpressure_ms": 250,
  "reconnect_backoff_initial_ms": 100,
  "reconnect_backoff_max_ms": 20000,
  "max_concurrent_reconnects": 2
}
```
Set conservative values first (lower buffer, pause shorter) and enable logs for `queue_length` and `reconnect_rate`.

patrick: FYI I opened PR 1234 that adds `pause_on_backpressure_ms` + basic circuit breaker for reconnect storms. Please review when you have a minute. :thumbsup:

maya: Nice — I'll try those SDK flags and run a short load with staging harness. If I still see parser errors I'll post a tiny repro client (should make debugging easier). Thanks! :pray:

jordan: Happy to run the staging job as well once you drop the repro link.

sam: Quick checklist to validate: [1] accumulate and only parse complete events, [2] add pause/resume around read loop, [3] exponential backoff + jitter + cooldown, [4] limit concurrent reconnects, [5] emit metrics for queue_length / parse_errors / reconnect_rate.

maya: Will report back after trying these. tagging @patrick for PR review ping.

patrick: Got it — I'll take a look this afternoon.

maya: Thanks everyone — follow-up thread incoming with repro and results.
